source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: St.Amant
entries.description: A Winnipeg organisation serving Manitobans with developmental disabilities and autism. For young children with autism it runs an Early Learning Program that builds life skills using applied behaviour analysis (ABA), and it offers case management for Manitoba families of children diagnosed with autism and clinical services such as outreach therapy for children.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Our Early Learning Program builds life skills using an approach called applied behaviour analysis (ABA).
entries.notes: CNAF lists St. Amant on its Alberta ABA page; it is in Manitoba. CNAF links to http://www.stamant.mb.ca/autism-services; that no longer works (the domain does not resolve). The organisation now uses https://stamant.ca/. Contact details from the home page footer. Case management is for families eligible for Manitoba's Children's disAbility Services.

entries.name: Children's disABILITY Services (CDS)
entries.description: A Manitoba Department of Families program for families raising a child under 18 who has an intellectual disability, developmental delay, autism or a lifelong physical disability. A Children's disABILITY Services worker helps the family plan and arrange supports, which can include case work, respite, therapy, basic funding for supplies, equipment and home or van modifications, and help with transportation costs. Families can apply directly with the referral and intake form and written confirmation of the diagnosis.
entries.cost_note: Government program; the pages do not mention fees. The amount of service depends on eligibility, assessed need and the program resources available.
entries.evidence: This program, provided through Manitoba Department of Families, supports families who are raising a child (or children) with developmental and physical disabilities, to meet some of the additional needs they may have.
entries.notes: Phone and email from the CDS home page; services from the Services and Supports page. Since 4 February 2025 families living in First Nations communities (on reserve) are eligible, and CDS now accepts autism diagnoses by community pediatricians for children aged 5 and under. Applications go to the regional CDS office. CNAF also listed a related FAQ page (Services and Programs for Children), dropped as an information page.

entries.name: Manitoba Human Rights Commission
entries.description: The provincial agency that administers Manitoba's Human Rights Code. It takes complaints of discrimination, investigates them and offers mediation, and provides human rights education and training. People can reach a human rights officer by phone, fax or email, or book an intake appointment at its Winnipeg or Brandon office.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention any fee for making a complaint.
entries.evidence: We take complaints of discrimination, investigate them and determine if there is sufficient evidence that The Code has been contravened to warrant a public hearing of the complaint.
entries.notes: Contact details from the site footer and home page. A home-page notice dated 21 August 2026 said a telephone line outage meant the office could not take calls and asked people to email hrc@gov.mb.ca. CNAF also linked a Manitoba government information page on the Human Rights Code (Human Rights and Reasonable Accommodations), dropped as an information page.

entries.name: Grants for Students with Disabilities (Manitoba Student Aid)
entries.description: Manitoba's student financial aid program for full-time and part-time post-secondary students. Students with a verified permanent, or persistent or prolonged, disability get the same loans, grants and bursaries as other students and may also qualify for the Canada Student Grant for Students with Disabilities and the Canada Student Grant for Services and Equipment. They self-identify on the MSA application and send a Verification of Disability form completed by a qualified medical assessor.
entries.cost_note: Loans and grants for students; the pages do not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: Students with a disability may be eligible to receive additional grants for each year of study.
entries.notes: Grant details from MSA's FAQ for Students with Disabilities; phone, email (for documents) and office address from the Contact Us page (in-person help Monday to Friday). The 2026-2027 application is open. The deadline to declare a disability is the midpoint of the study period. CNAF also linked a 2015-16 application form (404), dropped.

entries.name: Mind Matters Clinic
entries.description: A private practice in Winnipeg with clinical psychologists, social workers and counsellors who provide individual therapy, group therapy and psychological assessments for children, teens and adults. Its assessments include psychoeducational and ADHD assessments, autism screenings and mood evaluations.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed; the FAQ says group sessions cost less per session than individual therapy.
entries.address: 3-1250 Waverley Street Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada, R3T 6C6
entries.evidence: At the Mind Matters Clinic, we specialize in offering comprehensive psychoeducational ADHD assessments, autism screenings, and mood evaluations.
entries.notes: Address and phone from the contact page (open Sunday to Saturday, 8 am to 8 pm). The site shows its email only in disguised form (a Gmail address), so it is left out. CNAF lists the clinic twice (under Clinics who Diagnose and again under Speech and language Pathologists); the current team lists psychologists, social workers and counsellors but no speech-language pathologist.

entries.name: Red Ladder Optimized Learning
entries.description: An independent psychology practice in Winnipeg that offers psychological and psychoeducational assessments for children, teens and adults, at its Winnipeg offices and in communities around Manitoba. It diagnoses ADHD, learning disabilities, autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disabilities and other conditions, and offers intervention for learning-related concerns.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: We diagnose Attention Deﬁcit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), learning disabilities such as Dyslexia, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Intellectual Disabilities, and many other conditions, as well as emotional, relational, and stress-related difficulties.
entries.notes: All details from the one-page site (copyright 2023). CNAF links to http://redladder.ca/index.html, which now returns 400 Bad Request; the home page https://www.redladder.ca/ works.

entries.name: WELL Health Medical Centres – Manitoba Clinic
entries.description: A multi-specialty medical clinic in Winnipeg, founded in 1946 and now part of the WELL Health clinic network, next to the Health Sciences Centre. Its listed services include pediatrics, family practice, neurology and mental wellness therapy (in person and online), among other specialties.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: We are a multi-specialty medical clinic founded in 1946.
entries.notes: CNAF links to manitobaclinic.com; that domain now redirects to WELL Health's page for the clinic (wellclinics.ca). The page lists Pediatrics but does not mention autism assessments (CNAF says its pediatricians assess children for ASD); ask about referral and intake. The page says the clinic phone number changed to 431-482-9500.

entries.name: Early Learning Program (St.Amant)
entries.description: A provincially funded early intervention program at St.Amant for preschool-aged children in Manitoba who have an autism diagnosis and are eligible for Children's disABILITY Services. Children get one year of individualized behavioural intervention based on applied behaviour analysis, up to 20 hours a week in a St.Amant classroom (Winnipeg) or a partnering child care centre, in English or French, and families can attend the Fulfilling Potential workshop series.
entries.cost_note: The page says it is a provincially funded service; it does not mention fees.
entries.evidence: The St.Amant Early Learning Program is a provincially funded service for preschool-aged children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.
entries.notes: CNAF links to stamant.mb.ca (MABACA and the St.Amant ABA preschool program); that domain no longer resolves. The organisation now uses stamant.ca. Program details, Central Intake phone and email from the program page; address from the site footer; 'not-for-profit' from the About page. Children in rural Manitoba are served in partnering child care centres. The program now lasts one year (CNAF's text describes the older three-year program).

entries.name: Enhanced Consultative Services for students with autism (St.Amant)
entries.description: St.Amant Autism Programs consultants support the school team and family of students who completed the St.Amant Early Learning Program, at school or at home, through the school year and until the student graduates high school. Parents prepare the referral with the child's education team, and it must be approved by the school division.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Consultative services are available to school teams and families for students who have completed our Early Learning Program.
entries.notes: CNAF links to stamant.mb.ca/school-age-aba-program; that domain no longer resolves. The organisation now uses stamant.ca. CNAF describes a school-age ABA program with set weekly hours; the current service is consultation, open only to children who took part in the Early Learning Program. Central Intake phone from this page; email from the Early Learning Program page; address from the footer.

entries.name: Special Olympics Manitoba
entries.description: A charity that offers sports training and competition for Manitobans with an intellectual disability, from age two up. Volunteer-run community programs in all seven regions of the province cover 17 summer and winter sports, along with school, youth, health (Healthy Athletes) and athlete leadership programs; athletes register through their region.
entries.cost_note: The pages checked do not mention fees.
entries.evidence: Special Olympics Manitoba offers quality sports training programs and competitions to individuals with an intellectual disability.
entries.notes: Contact details from the site footer (provincial office in Winnipeg; toll-free 1 (888) 333-9179); som@ is the organisation's general address. Registration for new athletes for the 2026/2027 fall and winter season opened 9 September; an application does not guarantee a place.

entries.name: Winnipeg Speech-Language Services
entries.description: A private speech-language pathology practice run by Heather J. Shpak, a registered speech-language pathologist, for children and adults. It offers articulation, language development, phonological awareness and fluency (stuttering) therapy, tutoring for language-based subjects, and consultation for adults, in person in Transcona (Winnipeg) or virtually for anyone in Manitoba.
entries.cost_note: Private therapy; the site says many group insurance plans reimburse it and offers a free, no-obligation telephone consultation.
entries.evidence: Heather J. Shpak, registered speech-language pathologist, offers private one-on-one speech therapy in Winnipeg, Manitoba.
entries.notes: Phone and email from the site header (speech@ is the practice's address). The site works over https only without certificate checks, so the website stays http://. It still mentions COVID-19 measures (no visits to clients' homes). Children's page covers preschool and school-aged children.

entries.name: Children's Speech Language Pathology (Interlake-Eastern Regional Health Authority)
entries.description: The Interlake-Eastern Regional Health Authority's speech-language pathology program for Interlake children from birth to school entry, and for home-schooled children. It offers assessment, intervention, consultation, referrals and help with the move to school, at community health offices, nursery schools, daycares, homes or virtually. Parents can refer their own child through the Children's Therapy Network of Manitoba (CTNM) referral form.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: As a partner in the Children’s Therapy Network of Manitoba (CTNM), the program provides comprehensive speech-language pathology services to optimize the communicative health of Interlake preschool children.
entries.notes: CNAF links to ierha.ca/default.aspx?cid=6317, which now returns 404; the program's current page is on ierha.ca under Allied Health. Address and phone are for the Interlake CTNM Central Intake where referral forms go. CNAF's 'Interlake Children's Therapy Initiative' is now the Children's Therapy Network of Manitoba.

entries.name: Wirth Behavioural Health Services (WBHS)
entries.description: A private practice in East St. Paul, Manitoba, with psychologists, psychological associates, behaviour analysts and interventionists. It offers assessments and interventions for autism and ADHD, early intensive behavioural intervention (EIBI), support with complex behaviour, parent coaching, and social skills, sleep and toilet training, for infants through adults, in person or virtually.
entries.cost_note: The FAQ says rates follow the Manitoba Psychological Society's recommended fees; extended health plans may reimburse most fees, and WBHS does not direct bill.
entries.address: Unit #2 - 48 Ryan Wirth Way East St. Paul, Manitoba R2E 0R2
entries.evidence: psychologists, psychological associates, behaviour analysts, and interventionists who provide assessments and interventions for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
entries.notes: Listed on CNAF's Manitoba ABA sub-page. Address and phone (call or text) from the home page; ages and fees from the FAQ. The only email shown is a Gmail address, so it is left out (CNAF lists the owner's personal Gmail, which is not used).
